newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots mixed.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end down, spots mixed.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly down in lower volume on Friday after the top securities watchdog said it would assign supervisers to securities exchanges, traders said.
Traders said there were still many irregularities on the fledging markets and the assignment decision by the China Securities Regulatory Commission was seen as big negative news.
The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract fell to 11.00 percent from 11.49 percent on Thursday.
Turnover tumbled to 4.64 million lots from 12.73 million. One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
"The (assignment) news greatly hurt market sentiment," said one trader. "The repo rates are likely to move at lower levels next week."
But traders said more domestic A share issues and the active A share markets in Shanghai and Shenzhen were likely to support the rates.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mixed after moving in a narrow range for the whole session and traders said market sentiment was weak.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 rose slightly to 123.47 yuan from 123.18 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell to 1.54 million lots from 2.28 million.
Traders expect the contracts to continue moving in a narrow range around current levels early next week.
